overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any of the five allegations about the March 31 Billerica Select Board meeting, and declined to review concerns first raised in the request for further review.

allegations.summary: Chair failed to provide the complainant with documentation of the complaints to be discussed in the March 31 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that the Board provide Ms. Favreau with a copy of the complaints to be discussed.

allegations.summary: Chair did not allow discussion of the complaints before a motion and vote to hire an outside investigator.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any topic, nor does it establish requirements for the level of detail a public body’s discussions must include.

allegations.summary: Chair did not allow the complainant to defend herself against the complaints during the March 31 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: An individual who would have the rights afforded under Purpose 1 does not have analogous rights when the discussion is instead held in open session.

allegations.summary: Chair did not allow the complainant access to her legal counsel during the March 31 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Even if the discussion had been held in executive session, the Open Meeting Law would not have provided Ms. Favreau the right to have her counsel actively participate in the session.

allegations.summary: Notice for the March 31 meeting was insufficient because it did not say the Board would vote to hire an independent investigator into the complaints.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the notice topic indicating that the Board would discuss complaints against Ms. Favreau was sufficient.

allegations.summary: Additional concerns raised for the first time in the request for further review, not in the original complaint filed with the Board.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, several of the concerns, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
